subject: chemistry
title: Catalysts and enzymes
key_idea: A **catalyst** speeds up a reaction by providing a different pathway with a lower activation energy. It is not used up and the products stay the same. Enzymes are catalysts in living things.

blocks.text: This section covers the features of a catalyst and how to show that a substance is one.

items.meaning: A substance that speeds up a reaction without being used up.
A biological catalyst, found in living things.

items: A catalyst **increases the rate** of a reaction.
It is **not used up**: it is chemically unchanged and has the same mass at the end.
It does not change the products of the reaction.
It is not written in the chemical equation, because it is not used up.
Different reactions need different catalysts.

rows: Making ammonia in the Haber process
Removing nitrogen monoxide and carbon monoxide from car exhausts
The metal catalyst in a catalytic converter

blocks.text: Showing that a solid is a catalyst

items.text: Find the mass of the solid before the reaction.
Add it to the reaction and check that the reaction is faster.
Filter the mixture, wash the solid and dry it.
Find the mass again. If it is unchanged, the solid was not used up and is a catalyst.

items: A catalyst speeds up a reaction and is not used up.
Its mass is the same at the end, and the products do not change.
Different reactions need different catalysts.

blocks.text: A catalyst gives the reaction a different pathway. This pathway has a lower activation energy.

diagram.alt: Pick a type of reaction and whether a catalyst is used to see its energy profile.

items: The catalyst provides an **alternative pathway** for the reaction.
This pathway has a **lower activation energy**.
A greater proportion of collisions then have enough energy to react, so the rate increases.
The reactants and products are the same, so the energy change of the reaction is the same.
On a reaction profile, the catalysed line has a lower peak and starts and ends at the same levels.
(Higher tier) A catalyst does not change the position of equilibrium. It speeds up the forward and reverse reactions equally.
A catalyst gives an alternative pathway with a lower activation energy.
On a reaction profile the peak is lower. The start and end levels do not change.

blocks.text: Enzymes are the catalysts of living things. They speed up the reactions that keep an organism alive.

items: Enzymes act as catalysts in biological systems.
Yeast contains enzymes. They catalyse the reactions that produce alcoholic drinks.
Like other catalysts, an enzyme is not used up and does not change the products.
Enzymes are biological catalysts.
Enzymes in yeast are used to make alcoholic drinks.

checks.q: Explain how a catalyst increases the rate of a reaction.
checks.a: It provides a different (alternative) pathway for the reaction, which has a lower activation energy.

checks.q: A student adds 0.5 g of a black powder to hydrogen peroxide. The reaction speeds up. State how the student could show that the powder is a catalyst.
checks.a: Filter, wash and dry the powder at the end. Its mass is still 0.5 g, so it has not been used up.

worked_example.question: Explain the effect of using a catalyst on the rate of production of methanol.
answer_points: The catalyst increases the rate of the reaction.
By providing an alternative pathway for the reaction.
worked_example.tip: One mark each: the effect on the rate, the alternative pathway, and the lower activation energy.

worked_example.question:
Some reactions are affected by the presence of a catalyst.

Devise a simple experiment to find out what happens to the mass of a solid catalyst during a reaction.
answer_points: Use a known mass of the catalyst in a reaction (find the mass of the catalyst before the reaction).
After the reaction, remove the catalyst by filtering, then wash and dry it.
Find the mass of the catalyst afterwards. The mass is unchanged.
worked_example.tip: Any three experimental points score. Calculating the difference between the final and initial masses is also credited.

worked_example.question:
Most cars have catalytic converters which catalyse the reaction between nitrogen monoxide and carbon monoxide to make nitrogen and carbon dioxide gases.

Explain how the use of a catalyst in the catalytic converter increases this rate of reaction.
answer_points: The catalyst provides an alternative reaction pathway.
worked_example.tip: Reactants adsorbing onto the surface of the catalyst so that bonds are weakened earns 1 mark.

worked_example.question: State what is meant by the term catalyst.
answer_points: A substance that increases the rate of a reaction (M1)
and remains unchanged at the end of the reaction (M2)

blocks.text: (Supplement) Oxides of nitrogen are made in car engines and removed in the exhaust.

items: Nitrogen and oxygen from the air react together in the hot engine to make oxides of nitrogen, such as NO and NO₂.
A catalytic converter in the exhaust removes them, along with carbon monoxide.
Nitrogen monoxide and carbon monoxide react on the catalyst to make nitrogen and carbon dioxide.

blocks.label: In a catalytic converter
where: CO is carbon monoxide, NO is nitrogen monoxide
the products, CO₂ and N₂, are not polluting gases

worked_example.question:
This is the equation for the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide.

2H₂O₂(aq) → 2H₂O(l) + O₂(g)

The rate of reaction increases when a catalyst of manganese(IV) oxide is added.

A student adds 50 cm³ of hydrogen peroxide solution to a glass container and then adds 1.0 g of manganese(IV) oxide. The student waits until the hydrogen peroxide solution completely decomposes.

Describe how the student could then show that the manganese(IV) oxide was a catalyst and not a reactant.
answer_points: Reweigh it: the mass is still 1.0 g, so it was not used up (M3)

blocks.text: The effect of different solids as catalysts can be compared by timing the same reaction with each one.

items.text: Put a measured volume of hydrogen peroxide solution in a conical flask joined to a gas syringe.
Add a known mass of manganese(IV) oxide, put the bung in and start the stopwatch.
Read the volume of oxygen in the gas syringe at set times, or time how long it takes to collect a fixed volume.
Do the same with the same mass of copper(II) oxide, keeping the volume and concentration of hydrogen peroxide and the temperature the same.
The better catalyst makes more gas in the same time, or takes less time to make a fixed volume.
